export const meta = {
  name: 'aa5-explore',
  description: 'AA5: tune the lake-edge TAA toward reference glide, and root-cause the far-floe pale-block pop',
  phases: [{ title: 'Explore', detail: 'AA5a glide tuning, AA5b far-floe pop' }],
}

const X = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    track: { type: 'string' },
    implemented: { type: 'boolean' },
    switch: { type: 'string' },
    files_changed: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    root_cause: { type: 'string' },
    chosen_settings: { type: 'string' },
    metrics_table: { type: 'string', description: 'BASE / AA3 / yours / GT for every metric you used, per path' },
    perf_vs_base: { type: 'string' },
    gates: {
      type: 'array',
      items: { type: 'object', properties: { gate: { type: 'string' }, verdict: { type: 'string' }, numbers: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['gate', 'verdict'] },
    },
    images: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'slices / strips / crops the lead should look at, full paths' },
    patch_path: { type: 'string' },
    log_path: { type: 'string' },
    recommendation: { type: 'string', enum: ['adopt', 'adopt-with-fixes', 'reject'] },
    open_issues: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
  required: ['track', 'implemented', 'metrics_table', 'recommendation', 'patch_path', 'log_path', 'images'],
}

phase('Explore')
const res = await parallel(args.tracks.map((x) => () =>
  agent(`${args.common}\n\n${x.prompt}`, { label: `aa5:${x.key}`, phase: 'Explore', schema: X })))
const out = res.map((r, i) => (r ? { ...r, key: args.tracks[i].key } : null))
if (out.some((r) => !r)) log('an AA5 agent returned nothing')
return out

Quality tiers: T0 phones / iGPU (FXAA, plate lake, DPR 1), T1 desktop (MSAA 4, mirror lake LAKE_R12), T2 (MSAA 4, higher).   4. The half-float alpha view distance is too coarse for depth-based sub-pixel reconstruction near the camera.
  5. EnvEdge's silhouette blur is sigma 0.6 px at 1x, the GT's effective edge width is ~0.3 px: sigma 0.3 alone moved 56-72 % of changed pixels toward GT (solid-side error -12 %) but crawl got slightly worse (MC32 -59 % vs -61 %). 'A GT-like edge needs the narrower blur plus more temporal samples.'
  6. FAR-FLOE PALE BLOCK: on the medium path (frames ~52-200, x 190-250, y 499-506) BASE and AA3 show a pale block under the near floe where the GT shows the floe's dark reflection (mean luma 183 vs 166, single pixels up to 70 levels off) and it POPS in: x230 frame 51 -> 52 goes 117/148/160 -> 201/190/191. result.root_cause:
Why AA3 still stepped:
- Its TAA used a constant 0.5 history, about a 3-frame window. At slow sub-pixel speeds the 4 samples' coverage steps are many frames apart, so that window cannot bridge them.
- EnvEdge's 0.6 px silhouette blur was then added on top of the TAA output, making AA3's edges wider than the GT's (about 0.3 px effective).

What F1 changes: more history at slow pixel motion and no blur on the band while moving. Edges come out crisper and step less.

What limits it:
- The history is re-sampled with Catmull-Rom every frame, which softens the edge; at 0.85 at every speed the solid-side error grows 21-37 %.
- Silhouettes slide along curved surfaces, so their true motion is irregular; the GT shows the same irregular steps.
- Much of the remaining gap to the GT is not anti-aliasing: the GT's lake has only 0.68 of BASE's texture energy and different 2x reflections, and every 1x variant (BASE included) sits about 0.18 px toward the solid versus the GT because of the linear resolve.
- The far-floe pale blocks are a reflection difference and are unchanged in BASE, AA3 and F1.
result.perf_vs_base: Full (B + C) vs A only, measured in one session per build: glide +5.2..+5.5 %, AA3 +4.0..+4.5 % in the same conditions. The ~1 % difference is inside the noise of a heavily loaded machine. A alone is about 0.998 of BASE, so G7 stays as borderline as AA3's (+4.5..+5.9 % in its builder's quiet run).
open_issues: Plain answer: F1 does NOT yet glide like the GT. It is crisper and steps less than AA3. The clearest win is the FS slab edge (row 690 slices, slow and medium): AA3's lumps and small steps are gone and the edge advances like the GT's, only softer. On the WR, RS, FR and DR column slices F1 looks like AA3: both smoother than BASE, both short of the GT. Relative to the GT's own edge motion the jerk drops only 7-8 % from AA3; the GT edge is still narrower (1.92-1.94 px vs 2.22-2.23 px).

G4 on its literal reading: against the blurred TAA-off frame there are 90 px per Mpx-frame more than 4 levels outside, max 51. This comes from removing the band blur (balanced dark/bright: sharpening, not a rim); against the unblurred resolve it is 0.6. If the lead counts this, set the band sigma to 0.45 (tested on slow as AD1S45: solid-side 4.46, REL 0.241) or keep 0.6 (W85: crawl and glide better, edge softer).

G1's rule that J48 / J32 stay within 5 points of the GT's reductions is broken, for F1 and for AA3: on the fixed masks the TAA smooths band flicker more than the GT (slow J48: AA3 -76, F1 -78, GT -60).
Far floes: solid-side error vs GT rises (FF +15..21 %, FR +11..16 %) while FS and DR improve 10-26 %.

The far-floe pale blocks (lesson 6, a plausible part of the user's 'weird glitch') are a lake-reflection difference. They are visible in BASE, AA3 and F1 (reverse_FF strip, FF col 230 slices) and are untouched by this track.
G7 perf could not be resolved under the machine load: about +1 % over AA3, within noise.
Not separately tested: tab hidden -> visible and render-scale changes (AA3's restart / jump logic is unchanged), and a dedicated first-motion hitch check.

The patch keeps the explored lab-only knobs (step clamp, Keys a) behind ?debug; they could be stripped if the lead wants a minimal patch. Two small style leftovers: an IIFE when setting uGlideC.z in runTAA, and the Keys-cubic weights replace AA3's Catmull-Rom expression even at a = -0.5. Both were left as built so the verified build matches the patch.

Fixed masks and tools: capm.mjs blits the HDR resolve without post (no bloom) and gives linear coverage. glidecore / glide / glidesyn and the edge-width (ESF) and edge-speed bins are in the backup's tools/. Scratch caps under SP/work5/aa5a are wiped by a reboot.

result.track: AA5b: root-cause and fix the far-floe pale block that pops in (lesson 6) and other pops with the same cause. Product switch ?ffblock=0 gives AA3 exactly.
result.root_cause:
The block comes from the walk's face-colour lookup into T1's half-size mirror target (0.5 x 0.5, so 720x383). Directly under each face's foot, that target shows the floe's sunlit INSIDE. The mirrored camera sits under the water and looks into the floe through the oblique clip at the water line, and the double-sided bake shows the inside lit. The lookup sits only LK_HMIN = 5 cm (0.6 texel) above the foot, and its filter footprint is about 1 to 1.5 texels tall. At about 45 m a target row covers ~8.4 cm, so a far floe's face is only 1 to 2 rows tall and the lookup's taps reach the inside row. As the camera moves, the foot line slides across target rows. Every lake pixel whose walk reads that face texel (same heightfield cell, same uv) then turns pale at once, which gives a block with a sharp vertical edge that pops in.

Proof (debug renders, float readback, medium x230 y504-508, k51 to k52):
- The walk geometry is identical in both frames: Fc 0.72-0.96, parallax fraction 0.01-0.045, hM 0.05, uvM (0.809, 0.864).
- Only the first face's colour flips, luma 0.095 to 0.648.
- Dumping the mirror target there: the face rows are at path 46 m (luma 0.06-0.14) and the pale row directly under them is at path 48 m (luma 1.2-1.8, the inside). The lookup's bilinear taps put 25-31 % weight on that row.
- ?lkmscale=1,1 removes the block at this spot; ?lkhalf=0, ?lkwdiv=2 and ?lkwnear=0 do not.
- The 2x GT has its own pale block at k44-50 (x 186-194) by the same mechanism on a thinner face (hM 2-4 cm).
- The same block appears in the reverse sweep (k162-172 and others) and as a notch under the near floe on the slow path.
result.switch: ?ffblock=0. With it, the GLSL guard text is not inserted at all: the water, walk, cache and cacheN materials use WATER_FRAG itself. Checked with ident.mjs against the AA3 builder's JSONs: final image, every target and all 15 linked programs are identical to AA3. With all switches off it equals BASE. T0, ?envlake=plate and T2 are unchanged.
result.chosen_settings:
v3, in app/hero/engine/world/Water.ts only. The guard is inserted after the walk's face lookup (textureGrad) in lkWalkTerm. It applies only when the r12 heightfield walk runs and ffblock is not 0.

- Guard weight: gFt = (1 - smoothstep(1, 2, lowest tap above X's foot, in texels)) x (1 - smoothstep(2, 3, highest tap above X's foot)). It acts only on small footprints near the foot; X's foot projects onto the face at or above its true foot.
- Where it acts: the lookup point stays where the walk puts it. The two bracketing target rows are read with textureGrad (dy 0, same horizontal footprint). A row lying d metres of path farther than the nearer row takes the nearer row's colour, weight 1 - exp(-d / 0.3).
- Blend: cF = mix(AA3 colour, guarded colour, gFt), so nothing switches abruptly.
- Constants: LK_FFB 1 texel, LK_FFBT 0.3 m.
- Lab-only params: ?debug&ffb=, ?debug&ffbt=, ?debug&ffbtoggle=1 (run-time uniform for perf A/B, not in the product source).
- Rejected versions: v1 (move the lookup 1 texel up) put short faces' lookups over their top and added dark dashes and a bright column. v2 (two-row lookup on every near-foot footprint) put a pale haze on the lake before the right rocks.

result.perf_vs_base: The guard is about free: in one session with a run-time on/off toggle, the paired on/off median was 1.004 on medium (range 0.957-1.034; an earlier, noisier run gave 0.968) and 1.001 on fast. The machine was contended (frames 22-41 ms), so the noise is about ±3 %. The guard runs in the quarter-size walk pass and in the per-pixel walk along footprint edges. Versus BASE the total stays AA3's +4.5..5.9 % (not re-measured), plus about 0-0.4 %.
open_issues: The rest frame is not identical to AA3 / BASE: about 10.6k lake px per frame change by more than 4 lv (max 116), under the floes' waterlines and in faint reflection columns. The change moves toward the 2x GT (error 12.50 -> 8.96). A motion-only guard would pop when the camera stops, so this needs the lead's decision against G3's rest clause.
G4 as written is not met: the halo metric vs BASE's 3x3 rises from 591-1866 to 8001-9046 per Mpx because the reflection colours under the floes change. The strips show no rims or outlines.

Not fixed, different cause: small dark dashes at the far-left floe corner (x 85-160, y 530-575). The walk hits tiny objects on and off at heightfield resolution; they are present in BASE and AA3 too. Right-side events at x1094-1145 y680-711 and x940-1015 y745-765 are unchanged from AA3.
v3 adds a few small pops vs AA3: 736 / 386 / 1263 px on medium / slow / reverse (largest cluster 33 px), against 7798 / 2532 / 11297 px removed.
A face shorter than about one target texel still cannot be read cleanly: any lookup mixes in the inside or the background. The 2x GT has the same limit at its own scale.
Not measured for v3: fast, diag and leave paths; the G1c glide metric; G6 phase; tab hidden -> visible; render-scale changes.
The perf runs were contended (frames 22-41 ms, about ±3 % noise). Re-time in a quiet window if G7 needs a firmer number.

The reverse GT (caps/reverse_gt) and the bloom-free masks (caps/*_bmask) are in the scratchpad, which a reboot wipes. The backup holds the patch, LOG, images, tools and result files, not the captures.
